brief.title: Leave and Attendance System for Plant Workforce
business_goals: Consolidate attendance and leave management into a single system.
Automate punch-in/out data capture from existing biometric scanners.
Enable workers to apply for leave via a mobile app.
Implement a 24-hour supervisor approval workflow for leave, with automatic HR escalation.
Ensure leave and attendance data is locked and exportable by the 25th of each month for payroll.
Automate earned leave accrual calculation for factory workers as per Factories Act.
Provide supervisors with a shift-wise attendance dashboard.
Automate export of attendance and leave data to GreytHR for payroll.
Flag overtime (punch-out >30 minutes after shift) for manager approval.
Retain at least two years of attendance history for labour audits.
Ensure attendance status updates within 5 minutes of a punch.

stakeholders.name: Sunita Rao
concerns: Centralized system for leave and attendance

stakeholders.name: Vikram Singh
concerns: Accurate earned leave calculation for compliance

stakeholders.name: Deepak Joshi
concerns: Timely and accurate data lock for payroll (by 25th)
Automated and reliable data export to GreytHR
Eliminating manual errors from current leave process

stakeholders.name: Anjali Mehta
concerns: System performance and scalability (460 users, 5-minute updates)
Technical feasibility of biometric scanner integration

constraints: Must integrate with existing biometric fingerprint scanners; no hardware replacement.
System must be live before the next audit cycle in April.
Leave and attendance data must be locked and exported by the 25th of each month for payroll.
Must integrate with GreytHR for automated payroll data export.
Must comply with Factories Act for earned leave accrual (1 day per 20 days worked).
Must retain at least two years of attendance history for labour audits.
Attendance status must update within 5 minutes of a punch for 460 people.
Budget for the first year, including licensing, must be under 8 lakh rupees.
out_of_scope: Payroll integration for contract workers (only a simple log for compliance reporting is required).
open_questions: What are the technical specifications (e.g., API, data format) for integrating with the existing biometric scanners?
What are the specific requirements for the 'simple log for compliance reporting' for contract workers?
What are the exact data fields and format required for the automated export to GreytHR?
What are the detailed functional and non-functional requirements for the mobile application?

epics.title: Biometric Attendance Integration
epics.goal: Automate accurate attendance capture from existing biometric scanners and replace manual registers.

epics.title: Mobile Leave Application & Approval
epics.goal: Enable workers to apply for leave via mobile and streamline the supervisor/HR approval process.

epics.title: Automated Leave Accrual
epics.goal: Automate the calculation of earned leave accrual for factory workers to ensure compliance.

epics.title: Payroll Data Management & History
epics.goal: Ensure timely and accurate attendance and leave data for payroll processing and maintain historical records for audits.

epics.title: Supervisor Attendance & Overtime Tools
epics.goal: Provide supervisors with dashboards to monitor attendance and tools to manage and approve overtime.

epics.title: Consolidated Workforce Management
epics.goal: Establish a single, comprehensive system for all workforce attendance and leave, including basic logging for contract workers.

stories.title: Capture Biometric Punches
stories.i_want: punch-in/out data from existing biometric scanners to be automatically captured and reflected in the system
stories.so_that: attendance records are accurate and updated in near real-time, providing the digital foundation to replace manual registers.

acceptance_criteria.given: an existing biometric scanner is operational and configured for integration with the system
acceptance_criteria.when: a worker performs a punch-in or punch-out
acceptance_criteria.then: the system shall successfully receive the punch data and update the worker's attendance status within 5 minutes, making it visible in the system.

stories.notes: This story focuses on the backend data capture and near real-time update. The UI/reporting aspects of 'replacing manual attendance registers' will be covered in separate stories.

stories.title: Apply for Leave via Mobile App
stories.i_want: to apply for different types of leave (casual, sick, earned) via a mobile application
stories.so_that: I can easily request time off without using paper or WhatsApp

acceptance_criteria.given: I am logged into the mobile app
acceptance_criteria.when: I select a leave type (e.g., Casual, Sick, Earned) and dates
acceptance_criteria.then: my leave request should be successfully submitted to my supervisor for approval, and I should receive a confirmation message.

stories.title: Approve/Reject Leave Requests
stories.i_want: to approve or reject leave requests submitted by my team members
stories.so_that: I can manage my team's availability efficiently

acceptance_criteria.given: I receive a new leave request notification
acceptance_criteria.when: I review the request and approve it within 24 hours
acceptance_criteria.then: the worker's leave status should be updated to 'Approved' and the worker should be notified.

acceptance_criteria.given: I receive a new leave request notification
acceptance_criteria.when: I review the request and reject it, providing a reason
acceptance_criteria.then: the worker's leave status should be updated to 'Rejected' and the worker should be notified with the reason.

stories.title: Escalate Unapproved Leave to HR
stories.i_want: unapproved leave requests to be automatically escalated to me after 24 hours
stories.so_that: no leave request is left unaddressed

acceptance_criteria.given: a leave request has been pending with a supervisor for more than 24 hours
acceptance_criteria.then: the system should automatically escalate the request to HR, notify the HR administrator, and update the request status to 'Escalated to HR'.

stories.title: Calculate Earned Leave Accrual
stories.i_want: to automatically calculate earned leave accrual for factory workers
stories.so_that: compliance with the Factories Act is maintained and leave balances are accurate

acceptance_criteria.given: a factory worker has completed 20 days of work since their last accrual calculation
acceptance_criteria.when: the system performs the earned leave accrual calculation
acceptance_criteria.then: one day of earned leave should be accurately added to their leave balance and reflected in their leave statement.

stories.title: Lock Monthly Attendance & Leave Data
stories.i_want: leave and attendance data to be locked by the 25th of each month
stories.so_that: payroll processing can begin with final, unchangeable data

acceptance_criteria.given: it is the 25th of the month
acceptance_criteria.when: the system performs the monthly data lock
acceptance_criteria.then: the system should prevent any further modifications to attendance or leave data for the preceding period, and mark the data as 'Locked'.

stories.title: Export Locked Data for Payroll (Manual)
stories.i_want: to manually export the locked leave and attendance data in a generic format
stories.so_that: it can be used for payroll processing, backup, or manual verification

acceptance_criteria.given: the monthly data has been locked
acceptance_criteria.when: I initiate the data export from the system's interface
acceptance_criteria.then: a file containing the locked attendance and leave data, in a CSV format, should be generated and made available for download.

stories.notes: This story provides a manual, generic export option. It is dependent on S-006 (data locking). This is distinct from S-008 which focuses on automated integration with GreytHR.

stories.title: Automated Integration with GreytHR for Payroll
stories.i_want: attendance and leave data to be automatically transferred to GreytHR
stories.so_that: payroll processing is streamlined, and manual data entry into GreytHR is eliminated.

acceptance_criteria.given: the monthly attendance and leave data has been locked and is ready for payroll
acceptance_criteria.when: the scheduled automated export to GreytHR runs
acceptance_criteria.then: all relevant attendance and leave data should be successfully transmitted to GreytHR via its API, a confirmation log generated, and the data reflected in GreytHR.

stories.notes: This story focuses on the automated integration for core attendance and leave data transfer to GreytHR. It is dependent on S-006 (data locking). This is distinct from S-007 which provides a manual, generic export.

stories.title: Access Historical Attendance Data
stories.i_want: to access and retrieve at least two years of attendance history
stories.so_that: we can comply with labour audit requirements and review past records

acceptance_criteria.given: a request for attendance records from 23 months ago
acceptance_criteria.when: I query the system for historical data through the user interface
acceptance_criteria.then: the system should successfully retrieve and display the requested attendance history, confirming its retention.

stories.notes: This story focuses on the ability to retrieve and view historical data. The underlying data storage architecture to support this retention is a technical consideration that enables this story.

stories.title: View Shift-wise Attendance Dashboard
stories.i_want: to view a shift-wise attendance dashboard
stories.so_that: I can quickly monitor my team's presence and identify any discrepancies

acceptance_criteria.given: I am logged into the system as a supervisor
acceptance_criteria.then: I should see a clear overview of my team's attendance status for the current shift

stories.title: Flag & Approve Overtime
stories.i_want: the system to flag potential overtime when a worker punches out significantly after their shift
stories.so_that: I can review and approve it

acceptance_criteria.given: a worker punches out 35 minutes after their scheduled shift end
acceptance_criteria.then: the system should flag this as potential overtime, notify me, and present it for my approval on my dashboard.

stories.title: Consolidate Attendance & Leave Management
stories.i_want: a single, unified system to manage both attendance and leave for all workers
stories.so_that: I can streamline all related HR processes, ensure data consistency, and eliminate disparate systems.

acceptance_criteria.given: I need to manage a worker's complete time-off and work presence records
acceptance_criteria.then: I should be able to view and manage all their attendance and leave data from a single interface.

stories.notes: This story represents the overarching goal of system consolidation. Its completion is dependent on the successful implementation of all other attendance and leave management stories (e.g., biometric capture, leave application, accrual, reporting).

stories.title: Log Contract Worker Attendance
stories.i_want: the system to maintain a simple log of attendance for contract workers, separate from regular employees
stories.so_that: we can meet compliance reporting requirements without full leave/accrual management for them

acceptance_criteria.given: a contract worker punches in/out using a biometric scanner
acceptance_criteria.then: their basic attendance entry should be stored in a dedicated log for contract workers, visible to HR, without triggering full leave or accrual calculations.

stories.notes: This story assumes contract workers use the same biometric scanners for punch-in/out, but their attendance data is processed and logged differently due to simpler compliance needs.

gaps.description: The brief's open question asks for technical specifications (API, data format) for biometric scanner integration. While R-002, R-014, and S-001 cover the integration, the specific technical details are not defined, which is crucial for implementation.
gaps.suggested_question: What are the exact technical specifications, including API documentation, data formats, and communication protocols, for integrating with the existing biometric scanners?

gaps.description: The brief's open question asks for specific requirements for the 'simple log for compliance reporting' for contract workers. R-021 and S-013 cover this, but the definition of 'simple log' and its specific data points or reporting needs are unclear.
gaps.suggested_question: What specific data points need to be captured for contract workers in the 'simple log', and what are the reporting requirements for compliance?

gaps.description: The brief's open question asks for exact data fields and format for automated export to GreytHR. R-010 and S-008 cover the automated integration, but the precise data mapping and format are critical for successful payroll integration and are currently undefined.
gaps.suggested_question: Could you provide the exact data fields, their formats, and the required API or file structure for the automated export to GreytHR?

gaps.description: The brief's open question asks for detailed functional and non-functional requirements for the mobile application. R-003 and S-002 cover the basic functionality (applying for leave), but detailed UX, specific features, and non-functional aspects (e.g., offline capability, performance on different devices) are missing.
gaps.suggested_question: What are the detailed functional requirements for the mobile app beyond applying for leave (e.g., viewing leave balance, attendance history)? Are there any specific non-functional requirements like offline access, performance, or device compatibility?

gaps.description: R-020 explicitly states the system shall support casual, sick, and earned leave. While S-002 covers 'Apply for Leave via Mobile App', it doesn't explicitly mention supporting these specific leave types in its description, which is a key functional detail.
gaps.suggested_question: Does the 'Apply for Leave via Mobile App' (S-002) explicitly include the functionality to select and apply for different leave types such as casual, sick, and earned leave as per R-020?

gaps.description: Anjali Mehta (IT Manager) raised concerns about 'System performance and scalability' beyond the 5-minute update for 460 users (R-013). There's no explicit NFR or backlog item addressing general system scalability, response times for other operations, or overall performance under load.
gaps.suggested_question: Beyond the 5-minute attendance update, what are the expected performance metrics for other system operations (e.g., dashboard loading, leave application submission)? What are the scalability requirements for future growth in user base or data volume?

gaps.description: Brief Goal 8 and R-010 explicitly require automated export to GreytHR for payroll. However, backlog item S-007, which references R-007 (generic 'allow export'), is described as 'Export Locked Data for Payroll (Manual)'. This creates a conflict or ambiguity regarding the primary method of payroll data export.
gaps.suggested_question: Given that Goal 8 and R-010 specify automated export to GreytHR for payroll, what is the purpose of the 'Manual' export (S-007) for payroll data? Is it a fallback, or for other systems, or is there a misunderstanding of the automation requirement?

gaps.coverage_note: The backlog provides good coverage for most of the business goals and functional requirements outlined in the brief. Key areas like biometric integration, mobile leave applications, approval workflows, earned leave calculation, and historical data retention are addressed. Non-functional requirements related to specific performance (5-minute updates) and compliance (data retention, Factories Act) are also covered. However, there are several ambiguities regarding the detailed technical specifications for integrations (biometric, GreytHR) and the mobile application, which are highlighted as open questions in the brief but not fully resolved in the requirements or backlog. A significant conflict exists regarding the manual versus automated export of payroll data, which needs immediate clarification to ensure the core automation goal is met. General system scalability and performance beyond specific updates also appear to be a missing non-functional requirement.
